pr_body:
This PR adds the support of the OCTOSPI peripheral and driver on the stm32 devices

A new Kconfig is defined to enable this new driver for accessing the NOR flash octo spi memories.
The new stm32 flash driver for octospi is similar to the quadspi.
A sample application is also adatpted to test the driver :  samples/drivers/spi_flash

In this configuration, only the second instance (octospi2) is enabled, The driver is not yet designed for multi-instance.
The stm32l562 disco kit and b_u585 disco kit are available for testing.
Note that the NOR octo-flash which is on the disco kit  does respond to the SFDP (wrong value is given). 
So the **sfdp-bfp table** is given by the DTS of the mx25lm51245 NOR octo flash controller. 

No DMA transfer yet

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/44690

Requires the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_stm32/pull/122

Signed-off-by: Francois Ramu francois.ramu@st.com

Re-formatting the PR to introduce the octospi driver for stm32 MCUs. This version is given by the STM32Cube. Refer to the [AN5050 - Octo-SPI interface on STM32 microcontrollers](https://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/technical/document/application_note/group0/91/dd/af/52/e1/d3/48/8e/DM00407776/files/DM00407776.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.DM00407776.pdf)

Introducing 2 possible data modes (spi-bus-width) and 2 possible transfer rate (STR/DTR) through DTS.
Currently SPI STR and OctoSPi STR mode are supported.
The driver was tested on the disco stm32l562e_dk on a Micron MX25LM51245 octoSPI  NOR  flash  in **SPI/STR** and **OctoSPI/STR** modes with a sample like ./samples/drivers/spi_flash adapted for the ospi.
The SDFP is not given by the NOR flash : the command is not answered by the NOR of that board. This is still to be improved.
The NOR flash is able to answer to the ReadID command with : Manuf = 0xC2, Mem Type = 0x85, Density = 0x3A  

For memory configuration, only polling mode is used. DMA transfer is still to be added for NOR flash read/write operation.
Next steps to come:
- [x] check the OctoSPI DTR mode
- [x]  check the SDFP jedec operation
- [ ]   add the DMA transfer  (stm32l5x)
- [ ]   add the DMA transfer  (stm32u5x)
- [x]   adapt to other targets.

adding the **octoSPI** mode and double data rate **DTR**
set DTS node of the mx25lm51245: ospi-nor-flash
with
```
 		spi-bus-width = <8>;
		data-rate = <2>;
```

supports the b_u585i_iot02a board with octo NOR flash on SPI/OPI mode and STR/DTR data transfer
(no DMA transfer)

adding the SDFP table from the DTS because some NOR octo- flash are all 0xFF,
In that case it is needed to give the 
```
		sfdp-bfp = [
			53 46 44 50 06 01 02 ff
			00 06 01 10 30 00 00 ff
			C2 00 01 04 10 01 00 ff
			84 00 01 02 C0 00 00 ff
			00 00 00 00   ];
```

in the DTS of the ospi-nor-flash node.

The JES216 requires 9 dwords for the sdfp table (here set to 0)
That will make the erase type table correct for use in the setup_pages_layout(). In case the erase param is wrong (from the sdfp table, the  default value is SPI_NOR_SECTOR_SIZE)

Removing the CONFIG_DEBUG to run the sample test
reformat file to fix warnings

Testing the OPI/ST/DTR modes:
In the DTS of the mx25lm51245 flash controller, adjust the  SPI mode and data transfer :
```
 spi-bus-width = <8>;  /*  OPI mode  */
 spi-bus-width = <1>;  /*  SPI mode */
 data-rate = <2>; /* DTR */
 data-rate = <1>;  /* STR */
```
Note that spi-bus-width = <1> and data-rate = <2>; is not a valid combination

issue_context.title: ST kit b_u585i_iot02a and OCTOSPI flash support
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
ST kit b_u585i_iot02a has flash MX25LM51245GXDI005 connected to the OCTOSPI2. I was not able to find any support for Octo-SPI.  Currently kit's external flash can not be used. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add ST Octo-SPI support to the Zephyr.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
If Octo-SPI can be used as SPI (MISO/MOSI) then example configuration for MX25LM51245GXDI005 would be nice.

**Additional context**
Add any other context or graphics (drag-and-drop an image) about the feature request here.

Here you need to specify `Req2AckTime` because in the HAL driver there is an assert in `HAL_OSPIM_Config`: 
```
#define IS_OSPIM_REQ2ACKTIME(TIME)          (((TIME) >= 1U) && ((TIME) <= 256U))
```

It appears that when using the OCTOSPI2 instance, the OSPIMux is unchanged (left disabled)
So even with ospi_mgr_cfg.Req2AckTime ==0, the HAL_OSPIM_Config() returns HAL_OK
Setting `ospi_mgr_cfg.Req2AckTime = 1`, though (since 0 is not valid)
